prompt: This EUDA initial report on 2-MMC is cited for the figures below. Report each exactly as printed, and say 'not found' for any that is absent: (a) the number of powder cases and the total number of law-enforcement cases in 2013-2024, with the percentage; (b) the total quantity of powder seized and the quantity in 2024; (c) the total quantity and the number of imports into the Netherlands from India; (d) the number of drug-checking cases in which 2-MMC had been sold as 3-MMC, with the percentage; (e) the number of samples in the Netherlands from January to March 2025 that had been sold as 3-MMC. Do not quote any passage longer than 15 words.
answer:
**(a) Powder cases and total cases, 2013–2024:** 2,314 powder cases (96.5%) out of 2,397 total law-enforcement cases. The report states "Powders constituted 2,314 (96.5%) of all cases."

**(b) Powder quantity:** 45,832 kg (45.8 tonnes) total for 2013–2024, from 2,196 cases with reported weight. In 2024 alone, 33,207 kg (72.5% of the total) was reported. The 2024 data is preliminary.

**(c) Netherlands imports from India:** 148 imports totalling 44,417 kg, which the report says is 97% of all 2-MMC quantity.

**(d) Drug-checking cases sold as 3-MMC:** Approximately 1,500 cases (78.8%). The report says 2-MMC was "primarily mis-sold as 3-MMC" in these cases. The figure is approximate, and the report does not give its denominator.

**(e) Netherlands samples, January–March 2025, sold as 3-MMC:** 197 samples (92.9%), all powders. The report does not attribute this figure to the Netherlands by name, but it is the only country that could account for it, since Spain's single sample was sold as 4-MMC and the Netherlands reported 212 of the 213 samples.
